title: This Is My Father's World
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: By faith we understand how and why the world was made. Glory in your Father's world, and let every gift draw your eyes to the Giver.
exhortation: The world tries to convince us that faith is a silly thing, that it rests on nothing and we simply decide to have it. But this verse doesn't just say that by faith we believe. It says that by faith we understand. Those who know God have an amazing foundation: we understand how the world was made and why it was made. And that makes it glorious to be out in God's creation, knowing the God who made the world we walk in.

In the hymn "This Is My Father's World," you can see the joy of a man walking with eyes full of wonder and a big smile on his face, glorying in his Father's world. What a privilege it is as Christians to take so much joy in a world our God created, and to hope in the world to come. If this world is so beautiful even though it is wrecked by sin, what will the next one be like?

So as we go through our day, let's not let this beauty pass us by without giving glory to God, worshiping in our hearts and thanking him for a creation that provides for us and sustains us despite our fallen state. Let's glory in a God who loved us enough to create this beautiful world.
prayer: Lord, we worship you, the maker and creator of all things. Help us not to make your gifts a reason for idolatry. All the good things you give us, even our families, our children and our spouses, are not to be worshiped above you.

Like the author of that hymn, who saw that everything around him was your world, may every beautiful thing we see, every grace and every kindness in our lives draw our eyes to you in thanks and worship. Keep us from putting our roots deep into this earth and finding our satisfaction in the gifts instead of the Giver. May we look to you. And what greater gift could there be than your Son, Jesus, who gave himself up on the cross for the forgiveness of our sins? Thank you for all you've done, and for the testimony of who you are that surrounds us every day, if we would only see it. Thank you, Lord, for your good gifts.
